title: BIDMC respiratory objects at a fixed envelope scale
research_question: Does a rolling-envelope construction of the BIDMC impedance respiration signal, declared once and frozen, produce respiratory rising and falling occurrences whose peaks agree with the two annotators' breath marks across all 53 subjects, and if not, where does it disagree?
data_source: PhysioNet BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset, version 1.0.0, DOI 10.13026/C2208R; the RESP column of bidmc_NN_Signals.csv for subjects 1 to 53 at 125 Hz, 60,001 samples each.
time_semantics: Each row is one sample taken at an instant; consecutive rows are 8 milliseconds apart.
preprocessing_steps: respiration_smooth is the rolling maximum of respiration over smooth_window samples, then the rolling mean over smooth_window samples, shifted back by smooth_window samples so that it is a look-ahead envelope
respiration_change is the first difference of respiration_smooth
observations where respiration_smooth or respiration_change is undefined at the edges of a subject's record are excluded from the partition and counted in the validation report
object_definition: One row of the result is one trough-to-trough respiratory object: a rising occurrence together with the falling occurrence that follows it, with the peak at the last rising sample.
measurements: count of complete objects per subject
peak position of each object in samples
period between consecutive peaks in seconds
full excursion of the raw signal within the object
temporal symmetry of rise and fall durations
validations: states are mutually exclusive and cover every valid observation
the derived envelope matches the notebook construction row for row
provenance: contract fingerprint (SHA-256 of the canonical contract JSON)
featuregraph version, Python, numpy, pandas and scipy versions
git commit and whether the tree was clean
claim_limits: the study does not identify the physiological origin of any object
the annotators' breath marks are a comparison series, not a ground truth
nothing here estimates respiratory rate for clinical use
